summary: Both full halves inspected. The mark after the first B-c expression is cancelled in pen and its old semicolon remains doubtful. The cancelled opening fragment reads or equival. Before f-shriek the old f hook and lower right-facing r shoulder are separate regular typewriter shapes; the stronger reading is typed f replaced by r, independently confirmed. The blots after (7) and after the later B conceal their old characters. The left brace in (8), arrows, and inclusions are hand-filled. Following is handwritten, but the added a before morphism is typed above the line. The o of to overlies l, the n of terminology overlies g, and the initial a of as overlies p. In the new section, asphericity of has f corrected by a pen r. The shriek subscripts are readable but their provenance is not securely established by their heavy ink. Section98 starts with the number and no title.

The x between or and equival is a cancellation in the gap. The old fragment itself stops at equival; no ending is supplied.

A distinct lower right-facing r shoulder lies beneath the surviving f hook. Both have regular typewriter outlines, with the r darker at the lower shoulder. Independent inspection supports typed f-to-r correction and finds no pen evidence.
The brown/black pen hatching conceals the old character before the live typed comma. The draft comma cannot be recovered securely.
The left grouping brace is hand-drawn across the two typed conditions. Mark that provenance while preserving both lines and their alignment.
The inserted a has the regular typewriter bowl and serif and sits above the line; its placement slash is pen.
The o contains the old l vertical and upper serif. The overprint retains regular typed forms.
The n retains an old g lower loop and upper-right ear, comparable to the typed g-to-n correction on the preceding page.
The character after B is covered by irregular pen hatching and cannot be identified as a comma with confidence.
The old typed f has a surviving upper hook, while a continuous pen shoulder changes the live letter to r.
The a retains the descender and bowl of an old typed p.
